name: Boris
label: Southern Lord
lede: A Tokyo band took its name from a Melvins song, released an hour-long track and called it a single, and has spent three decades declining to repeat itself.

eras.title: A name from the Melvins, then a drum swap
eras.text: Boris forms in Tokyo in 1992 as a four-piece, borrows its name from a Melvins track and loses its drummer by 1996. Atsuo moves to the kit, and the trio that results is still the core of the band.

years.h: A Tokyo band borrows its name from a Melvins track
years.p: Atsuo sings, [[Wata|0f61b915-11d8-4d09-b986-42280394c4ab]] plays guitar, Takeshi plays bass and Nagata drums. The name comes from a song on the [[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]] album Bullhead.
years.xp: Invisible Oranges reports the trio took the name "allegedly because of their appreciation of one of Dale Crover's drum fills." The Melvins and Earth, slow and heavy, were the starting template.

years.h: Boris calls its 60-minute Absolutego a single
years.p: Released on the band's own Fangs Anal Satan label, one track runs 60 minutes and 15 seconds. The band has always said it is a single, not an album.
years.xp:
It is the first release after drummer Nagata left, with [[Atsuo|6adc77be-0df7-4818-ab6c-3faf11bbf709]] now on the kit. Wikipedia notes Takeshi was credited as "Ohtani" on the 1996 release, corrected on later pressings.

Southern Lord reissued it in 2001 as Absolutego+ (Special Low Frequency Version), remixed and stretched to 73:24, with new Stephen O'Malley artwork of a Medusa-styled Wata. A 2020 reissue went back to the 1996 specs, with Third Man handling vinyl worldwide.

years.h: Atsuo takes over the drums after Nagata leaves
years.p: The band carries on as Atsuo, Wata and Takeshi, and that trio is still the core of Boris.
years.xp: With Atsuo behind the kit, Wata widened out to lead guitar and keyboards and Takeshi took bass and rhythm guitar. Since 2019, per Wikipedia, Atsuo has moved to the front on stage, with a rotating line of touring drummers.

eras.title: Long, low, and never the same twice
eras.text: The early records are slow and enormous, then the band cuts a rock album to tape in one take and a 43-minute feedback piece. Keiji Haino arrives as the first of many collaborators, and Southern Lord starts putting Boris out in America.

years.h: Amplifier Worship gives Takeshi the mic
years.p: Five tracks and 63:52 on the Tokyo label Mangrove, released November 26, 1998. It is the first Boris record with Takeshi on lead vocals.
years.xp:
Atsuo still sings lead on one track, "Huge." The record was made at Sound Crew in August and September 1998.

Southern Lord reissued it on CD in 2003 in a green jewel case, and some copies came with an edible gummy worm in the spine. Rumors that the worms were hallucinogenic were denied by Southern Lord, the band and people who ate one, according to Wikipedia.

years.h: Black: Implication Flooding pairs Boris with Keiji Haino
years.p: The 1998 record puts the band beside the Japanese experimental musician Keiji Haino, the first of many collaborations.

years.h: Critics skip Flood, a 70-minute piece in four movements
years.p: Recorded in September 2000 at Bazooka Studio and released on MIDI Creative, it starts with mechanical noise and ends in ambient quiet.
years.xp:
Part I is mechanical noise and looping guitar, Part II ambient, Part III a climactic layering, Part IV ambient minimalism. Wikipedia says critics overlooked it on release, and it grew into a cult record.

Boris played the whole thing every night of a 2013 US residency tour. Third Man pressed it on vinyl in 2021, and it reached streaming services on December 15, 2025, its 25th anniversary.

years.src: Wikipedia: Akuma no Uta · Invisible Oranges
years.h: Akuma no Uta goes to tape in one take
years.p: Cut January to March 2003 at Peace Music on analog tape. Pitchfork later put it at number 198 on its list of the top 200 albums of the 2000s.
years.xp:
The Diwphalanx original runs 31:59; the 2005 Southern Lord edition runs 39:00. Its cover pays homage to Nick Drake's Bryter Layter, with Takeshi holding a double-neck Ibanez where Drake had an acoustic guitar.

Southern Lord's picture disc came in two designs: 700 copies with the Drake art and 300 in a Venom-style cover. Invisible Oranges calls the record "the high-water mark of Boris's discography," and Wikipedia cites Mojo saying it sounds like a blueprint for every future Boris release.

years.h: Feedbacker, one piece, 43 minutes
years.p: Released on Diwphalanx in 2003 as five movements. Boris later played it whole at All Tomorrow's Parties in 2009 and 2010.

eras.title: Hot pink, Sunn O))) and an audience abroad
eras.text: A pink record with a fuzz-pop heart reaches Western ears, and a team-up with Sunn O))) follows on Halloween. Boris is soon opening for Nine Inch Nails.

years.h: Japan gets Pink first, and the West catches up a year later
years.p: Boris produces Pink itself at Sound Square, released November 18, 2005 by Diwphalanx. Southern Lord reissues it in 2006 with new artwork and a longer running order.
years.xp:
The Southern Lord CD runs 55:23 against 47:23 for the Japanese one, and swaps the stencil cover for William Blake's Satan illustrations, with perforated blotter-paper sheets in the package. Pitchfork gave it 8.7 and Spin an A; AllMusic gave it five stars. Stylus Magazine gave it a C, citing an infatuation with kitschy artistic jest.

The Nashville Scene called it the album that made metal hip. "Farewell" later turned up in Jim Jarmusch's The Limits of Control, and Boris toured the record's 10th anniversary in 2016 with Earth.

years.h: Boris and Sunn O))) release Altar on Halloween
years.p: Southern Lord puts out seven tracks recorded with guests including Kim Thayil, Joe Preston, Jesse Sykes and Dylan Carlson.
years.xp:
The record ends with "Her Lips Were Wet With Venom," 28 minutes and 14 seconds long, after the 14-minute "Blood Swamp." Pitchfork gave it 6.6 and PopMatters 8/10.

Invisible Oranges calls it "arguably the album most responsible for Boris's breakthrough in the US." The two bands played it with its guests at the London Forum on December 10, 2007, where 500 picture discs were sold.

years.h: Pink makes the year-end lists
years.p: It lands at number 9 on Pitchfork's Top 50 Albums of 2006 and tops Exclaim!'s metal readers' poll, according to Wikipedia.
years.xp: It later placed number 69 on Cokemachineglow's 100 best albums of the 2000s and number 20 on Treble's best metal albums of the 21st century.

years.h: The band calls Smile its sell-out album
years.p: Michio Kurihara and Stephen O'Malley guest. Boris told Terrorizer the record was "un-cool" and "the sell-out album."
years.xp:
Diwphalanx released it in Japan and Southern Lord in the US, with different art and track listing; the Southern Lord CD came with a bonus DVD of three music videos. It reached number 20 on Billboard's Top Heatseekers chart, and it is only the second Boris album with vocals on every track.

Reviews were cooler: Pitchfork gave it 6.4, and Invisible Oranges later called it "sprawling, unfocused."

years.h: Boris plays arenas for Nine Inch Nails
years.p: The trio opens for [[Nine Inch Nails|b7ffd2af-418f-4be2-bdd1-22f8b48613da]] on the Lights in the Sky tour in North America, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: Whole albums on stage
eras.text: Boris plays entire records live, lands a song in a Jim Jarmusch film and moves between labels. Michio Kurihara of Ghost sits in as a guest guitarist, and collaborations with Merzbow and Ian Astbury keep coming.

years.cap: Boris and Sunn O))) play Altar at All Tomorrow's Parties New York
years.h: Boris plays Feedbacker start to finish at ATP
years.p: The full 43-minute piece gets performed at All Tomorrow's Parties in 2009, and again at the 2010 edition curated by Pavement.

years.h: Jim Jarmusch puts "Farewell" in The Limits of Control
years.p: The Pink track plays in the 2009 film, and Jarmusch has a view on how the band works live.
years.xp: Jarmusch said that when Boris plays live, "they're in the mode ... of jazz musicians," listening to each other and building on each other's contributions.

years.cap: Wata at the Biltmore, Vancouver, October 11, 2011
years.h: New Album goes J-pop, on a new label
years.p: Its US release starts a run on Sargent House that lasts through Noise in 2014 and Dear in 2017.

years.h: Boris plays all of Flood every night of a US residency
years.p: The four-movement 2000 album anchors the whole tour, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Noise arrives with a North American tour behind it
years.p: Released June 17 internationally on Sargent House. Pitchfork gave it 7.8.

eras.title: Thirty years, and a record meant as a goodbye
eras.text: The 25th anniversary album is written as a possible last word, and the band decides to carry on instead. The pandemic splits a new project into a rock record and an ambient one, and Heavy Rocks becomes a title for the third time.

q: We wanted to create music that we could leave behind.
years.h: Boris makes Dear as a goodbye, then keeps going
years.p: Takeshi on what the 25th anniversary album was for. Released July 14, 2017 on Sargent House, with ten tracks on the final cut.
years.xp:
Bandcamp Daily dates the doubt to late 2014, when personal circumstances threatened the band's future. Takeshi said the aim was to leave something behind, and the sessions went so well they produced enough material for three albums. The rest was held for later.

Takeshi described how the trio works as "climbing a spiral staircase," and said the sound needs these three members. Metacritic scores it 78; AllMusic's Thom Jurek called them "rock leviathans."

years.h: Boris splits NOW into a rock album and an ambient one
years.p: NO comes out in 2020, self-released, and W follows in 2021.

years.h: A third Heavy Rocks, for the 30th anniversary
years.p: Relapse releases the album after earlier records with the same title in 2002 and 2011.
years.xp: It is the band's 27th studio album, 41 minutes and 34 seconds, with singles "She Is Burning," "Question 1" and "My Name Is Blank." AllMusic's Thom Jurek wrote that Boris "continue to willfully and eagerly engage a tense musical restlessness."

years.h: Fade shows up with no warning
years.p: The drone metal record arrives in the same year as Heavy Rocks, a surprise release, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: Looking back at the first records
eras.text: Boris revisits its earliest work: the 25th anniversary edition of Amplifier Worship lands in 2024, with new art built on the old gummy worm.

years.h: Amplifier Worship turns 25, and the gummy worm comes back
years.p: The anniversary reissue's new art, by Arron Horkey, is built on the gummy worms that came in the 2003 Southern Lord jewel case.
years.xp: Third Man released the 25th anniversary edition. Boris said the art came from Horkey's own memory of the worms in the jewel case when the CD came out.

sources.title: Invisible Oranges: So Grim So True So Real: Boris
